irreducible_incompleteness_analysis.description: Root-cause analysis and irreducibility determination for key mathematical incompleteness targets.

analysis_log.analysis: The transport operator NavT aggregates contributions from the non-local CSI domain. This summation is inherently many-to-one. No refinement of metric or window can recover the specific path history from the resulting CSI state.

The projection operator Pi_A maps all sub-threshold states to zero. At the exact boundary epsilon=0, the derivative of the projection is undefined. While renormalizable via epsilon-delta techniques, the information loss for states exactly at the threshold is irreducible.

Proving stability for all N steps does not automatically extend to the N->infinity limit without a specific asymptotic bound. Current support is simulation-based and finite; global closure requires an asymptotic assumption.
In systems with exact process symmetry, degenerate minima must result in multi-branch retention to preserve symmetry invariants. Forcing uniqueness would introduce unphysical bias.
Process branching is a primitive dynamic. The resulting multi-valuedness is not a lack of definition but a property of the deltaActualization operator.
Observables are low-dimensional projections of high-dimensional state histories. Information loss during projection prevents unique recovery of the underlying preimage.
The current lack of measure-theoretic structure is a gap in formalization, not an intrinsic limitation. Sigma-finite measure definition will resolve current discrete projection fragilities.
